3.happening: We count the elements as n = {n}.
3.why: Both loops range over all indices.

4.happening: We start result as an empty list.
4.why: One product will be appended per output slot.
4.invariant: result grows one slot at a time, left to right.

5.why: Each slot's value is the product of every other element.
5.invariant: Slots before i are already computed.

6.happening: We reset the running product to 1.
6.why: 1 is the identity, so it does not change the product.
6.invariant: prod holds the product of the elements considered so far.

7.happening: We sweep index j = {j} as a possible factor.
7.why: Every element except the slot's own is multiplied in.
7.invariant: prod includes all considered j != i so far.

8.happening: Index {j} is not the slot itself, so it is a factor.
8.why: The product excludes only the slot's own element.
8.invariant: nums[i] is never multiplied into slot i's product.

8.happening: Index {j} is the slot itself, so it is skipped.
8.why: 'Except self' means the element at i is left out.
8.invariant: The slot's own value is excluded.

9.happening: We multiply nums[{j}] into the running product.
9.why: It is one of the 'other' elements for this slot.
9.invariant: prod is the product of every j != i seen so far.

10.happening: We store prod = {prod} into result for slot {i}.
10.invariant: result now has this slot's product.

11.invariant: result[k] is the product of all elements except nums[k].

init.happening: Count elements and prepare an empty result.

loop.happening: Pick an output slot or sweep a factor.
loop.why: Each slot multiplies every other element.
loop.invariant: Slots and factors are visited in order.

update.happening: Multiply a factor or store a slot's product.
update.why: The product builds up then is recorded.
update.invariant: State reflects one slot's running product.

check.invariant: nums[i] is never a factor of slot i.
